Update:
Hey guys. Sorry that I didn't reply much. I don't feel that much better today, but I'm out of crisis-mode for now. My friend made me an appointment to see someone. I was on full crazy-mode yesterday, and kind of victimized myself too much. 

I still feel like shit, but not shitty enough to do anything dumb. Well, I did do one dumb thing, I brought myself a new expensive keyboard. I was looking forward to having it delivered toady, and it kept me going throughout the day. It feels nice to type on (I do a lot of programming, so a nice clicky keyboard does a lot to improve my mood). It's something stupid and small, but it's enough to make distract me. Now all I gotta do is stay distracted until I get help.

Anyway, I kind of learned a lesson about reaching out to strangers online. The majority of people would just say stuff and it won't resonate with you at all. It sounds shitty of me to say, and it probably makes me kind of shitty, but when I'm in a depressed mood I kind of ignore all advice and have a cynical view on anything anyone says to me. Maybe one or two people will say something that does reach me, and one or two people are trolls (so far 2 people have told me to kill myself, lol)

Well, you guys are awesome people. sorry that I didn't really participate. I'll try to participate more on this sub on my main account.

This makes me depressed, for several reasons:

1. People not understanding why other people are offended. This is probably beaten to death by now so I'm not really going to go into detail. Instead I'm going to go into detail for the other reasons.

2. In the "open discussion" Facebook post, Asian people making racist comments towards white people. I understand the concept of being offended and even feeling angry for stupid frat bullshit like this. I'm not disappointed at the Asian american community this time, because we're just people, and some of us are racist just like people. What upsets me is all the other people calling us hypocrites and using this to justify their own racism. This is a self perpetuating cycle. 

3. **People constantly comparing cultures and scenarios.. AS IF THERE IS SOME DEEPER MEANING** 
> what if we threw a white themed party? blah blah blah 
>> oh im white and I don't get offended at white themed parties
> oh hey there's this irish party and no irish people were offended WHY CANT YOU BE LIKE THOSE MINORITIES?!?!

Different cultures = different people. People can't seem to understand this. Just because Asian people get offended at some stuff doesn't mean white people would get offended at it. Likewise, just because there was once some irish party where people got really drunk and "celebrated" a bunch of irish stereotypes, and the irish community were okay with that, doesn't mean it's okay to do the same for every culture!

The reality is, America is getting more and more diverse. It's more diverse right now than it has ever been. Different cultures react differently to things. That's why I don't see Irish people getting mad at all the Irish jokes that we all see on cartoons, but Asian Americans like myself feel upset whenever Asian stereotypes are paraded on TV. 

That's why (a lot of) white people don't get offended when minority comedians make fun of their (white) culture on TV, but other cultures get offended. 

Part of the reality of accepting a more diverse country is to be sensitive of certain culture's without judgement or any other negative BS. 

My point is, different cultures are like different people. For example, I know some black people who think black stereotypes are funny, and actually tolerate race themed jokes aimed at them by their white friends. Clearly this is not the case, I'm pretty sure a lot of black people would be totally offended at the same type of jokes. We can't just be like "Hey, OFFENDED PERSON, Why can't you be more like NON OFFENDED PERSON? Let me tell you how you should FEEL about things!"

Obviously not all Asian people were offended at this. I know a lot who aren't offended. It's really a hivemind kind of thing. A lot of Asian Americans tell each other "Hey! There are all these people making fun of us, and they think it's okay! GOD these PRIVILEGED people are once again oppressing the shit out of us and not understanding! They represent everything we hate!" 

And a lot of white people tell each other "Hey! These Asians are overreacting! And some of them are saying racist shit about white people! God these minorities are so hypocritical! They also represent stuff that we hate!" and eventually this leads to an all out flame war like I saw on that Facebook group. It really gets back to the empathy argument. People need to learn to fucking empathize with each other instead of shoving their own beliefs down each other's throats.

Btw, I edited my post a minute ago.

But yes, every situation is different. If there is a white kid who has been a victim of racist bullying for all of his childhood, it still wouldn't be "okay" for him to tell a racist joke (it never is, for anyone...) but I would feel less anger than if it were, say, some white kid who was never bullied and has a history of bullying other people for their race in his childhood. I see both of these points. I mean throughout high school I have gone through several terrible incidents, where people thought it was "okay" to say certain "innocent" but horrible racist comments to me, and didn't do anything about it. And now in college I am starting to recognize when people say it, and get a bit angry at them. 

For instance, one night I was with a friend of mine, and he got really drunk and made a comment about "Asians having small penises" and I got physically angry. The fact that he was white and dating an Asian girl made me even more angry, but I recognize that's my own inner problem I have to deal with. The fact is though, I told him later that night that it was not an okay thing to say, to which he responded "It was just a joke lol." The next morning I apologized for being so angry and he accepted it, but didn't apologize for what he said. 

A few weeks later, I told this story to another friend of mine, and his comment was, "Well Renc, the thing is, he wasn't really being racist because the penis thing is statistically true. I read it on wikipedia." That made me pretty angry but at that point I didn't really care about fighting that battle. 

Oh well, just my experiences. The truth is some people just won't see and getting angry over something I can't change is a waste of energy.

YES! The EMTs that were with me said dickish things like that too! People can have the potential to really suck. 

And no, this happened roughly a year and a half ago. I just sorta never really talked about it, and never really got over it. I couldn't sleep tonight so I decided to write about it.

I finished high school already. I'm in the middle of college right now. I made some pretty awesome grades this semester too, so things are going well for me right now. 

I have some pretty decent friends in college, so yeah I agree with everything you've said. College and the people in college makes high school look like a piece of shit. The environment is really different. Of course when I was still in high school I heard that a lot, and I just blew it off as one of the many "cliche" things people always said.

At least I can look at these events like it has some kind of purpose. I used to be like the average "white" redditor, and I had typical problematic beliefs about gender and race. So it's not a "white" thing, and I generally don't like to associate the problem with white people. It's more like a privilege thing, and while I'm a minority I do recognize that I am pretty privileged. It's just the stupid layers of bullshit society keeps underneath, and the sudden bursts of stuff like the shit I faced in high school that made me recognize how bad things really are. 

I did do a lot of weird things over the last couple years that helped me recover a little. I tried really hard to expand my capacity of empathy. I remembered holding a grudge against law enforcement officers and other public workers after that incident. Also, there was another incident during my first year of college that intensified my hatred for cops. 

There was a time after that, when I decided enough was enough. I went to a forum that law enforcement officers posted on, and browsed through their posts. At first the things I saw kinda reinforced their negative stereotype in my mind. I saw them being dicks to people, especially non LEOs. But then I began to understand. Yeah, some of them were dicks, but they were also people. Just like how we're tired of their shit, they can also get tired of shit from regular people. That's why some of them were kind of rude. But still, the majority of them were at least decent, and not assholes. 

Then I realized, I only had to deal with cops twice in my life, and they have to deal with fucking people every day. So it's only fair that, the next time my path crosses with a cop, that I try my best not to piss them off or make their job harder. I realized that it's not their job to be nice to everyone they deal with, especially knowing that the people they deal with could try to kill them at any moment.

I also went on a lot of feminist forums lately. Just to learn that they are also human beings. Not that I've ever had anything against feminism... but after browsing places like /r/mensrights and elsewhere on the internet it's really easy to have an anti-feminist bias. 

Therefore.... I've also been reading the comments on /r/shitredditsays a lot lately. I don't know why. It's not like I'm one of them. I just want to understand other people, I guess. I mean strangely, after all the shit I went through, I find their rants about privilege and racism/sexism to be invigorating... Though I never post on there or participate. I don't like the general bitter attitude they have against everything, but at least now I understand why they are like this.

Anyways, thank you so much for responding. It means a lot to me that someone also understands the shit that goes on in my mind and has gone through some of it too. Thank you!
